messages:
Ellen: quick thread: proposing a "fallback credit" and "soft-quarantine" model in the manifest so runtime can make cost-aware, predictable fallbacks across hosted/dedicated/private. sketch and rationale below.

Marco: love the idea. we've had surprise billing when controlplane routed large batches to hosted variants during outages. a credit system could cap cost impact.

Tess: how would "fallback credit" work? is it per-tenant, per-variant, or global? also privacy concerns for private installs.

Rohit: proposal: manifest fields (minimal): capability_v:2, trust_band: public|tenant_isolated|hardware_isolated, allowed_ops:[...], fallback_credit_token (short string), soft_quarantine_window (seconds), spillover_policy: none|to_dedicated|to_hosted. and a cb_sla hint like "cb=errpct:10|min:50".

Ellen: semantics: fallback_credit_token ties to a small prepaid budget (ms or token units) the controlplane can spend on costlier fallbacks for that adapter before alerting the tenant. If absent => default zero. Helpful for short-term relief during incidents.

Marco: nice. runtime rules: if trust_band==hardware_isolated => spillover_policy must be none and allowed_ops cannot include kv_share. If controlplane attempts prohibited spillover, return 409 + code ERR_SPILLOVER_FORBIDDEN.

Tess: soft_quarantine_window: when a manifest changes (new epoch) runtime delays any auto-fallbacks for that tenant for N seconds, using local-only fallbacks first. reduces oscillation during rolling upgrades.

Rohit: also add an observability_hint: none|summary|stream. if none, controlplane must not expect per-request telemetry and should mark tenant as "telemetry_limited" in UI. adapters with observability_hint==none should expose a local admin endpoint to fetch audit logs.

Ellen: cost accounting: when a fallback occurs and it consumes fallback_credit, emit a small header X-RW-Fallback-Credit: "used=12|left=88|ticket=Ab3c" and a compact envelope bodybase64 for audit. If no credit, emit X-RW-Fallback-Credit: "none".

Marco: ops: add regional safety limiter: controlplane can only spend up to M credits per region per minute to avoid cascade spend. defaults TBD. Also require a manifest field capability_ttl so controlplane knows how long the credit assertion lasts.

Tess: SDK implications: when ERR_SPILLOVER_FORBIDDEN or ERR_FALLBACK_FORBIDDEN is returned, SDK should expose a SmallFallbackError with fields {code, denied_op, manifest_epoch, ticket}. Keep error payload small and typed.

Rohit: sample inline manifest snippet for discussion (kept small):
```json
{"capability_v":"2","epoch":"2026-04-01T12:00:00Z","capability_ttl":"900","trust_band":"tenant_isolated","allowed_ops":["generate","embed"],"fallback_credit_token":"cred:wx3","soft_quarantine_window":"30","spillover_policy":"to_dedicated","observability_hint":"summary","cb":"errpct:10|min:100"}
```

Ellen: soft-quarantine behavior: runtime prefers local fallback targets for soft_quarantine_window seconds; after window, it obeys fallback_sequence/spillover_policy. If manifest_epoch changes during window, reset window.

Marco: UI: show per-tenant "fallback credit" balance + ledger entries (time, consumed, remaining, ticket). show an amber badge when soft-quarantine active. 

Tess: privacy: for hardware_isolated tenants with observability_hint==none, credit tokens may be managed offline by support. controlplane shows "credit unmanaged" and will not auto-spend.

Rohit: circuit-breaker tie-in: if fallback_error_rate exceeds cb thresholds, runtime moves tenant into short "auto-block" where no further controlplane-initiated fallbacks happen for N seconds. record reason and emit event to UI.

Ellen: testing: dry_run flag to simulate spending credit and generating envelope without actually switching traffic. opt-in per tenant for canaries.

Marco: final note: manifest_signature + epoch remains critical to avoid drift; on mismatch, emit manifest_mismatch event and enter soft-quarantine until resolved.

Tess: I'll sketch SDK error shapes and a tiny UI mock. @Ellen can you fold this into the RFC diff?

Ellen: yes, I'll draft RFC section: vocabulary (trust_band, fallback_credit_token, soft_quarantine_window, spillover_policy, capability_ttl, observability_hint, cb string), runtime rules (deny kv_share for hardware_isolated, credit spending semantics, soft-quarantine), error codes, headers, and UI expectations. ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: pinned to #architecture for follow-up.
